title: Raoult's Law

references.label: NCERT Chemistry Part I, Class 12 — Solutions

expression: P(solution) = x(solvent)·P°(solvent)   [for a non-volatile solute; for two volatile liquids: P(total) = xₐPₐ° + x_bP_b°]
explanation: Raoult's law states that the partial vapour pressure of a solvent above a solution is proportional to its mole fraction in the solution, scaled by the pure solvent's vapour pressure. Adding a non-volatile solute lowers the solvent's mole fraction, and therefore lowers the solution's overall vapour pressure compared to the pure solvent — this relative lowering of vapour pressure is itself a colligative property, directly proportional to the mole fraction of solute. Result is expressed in Same pressure unit as P°. Conditions/assumptions: Ideal solution behavior is assumed; real solutions with strong solute-solvent interactions show positive or negative deviations from Raoult's law

variables.meaning: Mole fraction of the solvent in the solution
Vapour pressure of the PURE solvent at the same temperature

workedExample.scenario: A solution has solvent mole fraction 0.9, and the pure solvent's vapour pressure is 100 mmHg.

commonMistakes: Using the SOLUTE's mole fraction instead of the SOLVENT's mole fraction directly in the P = x·P° formula.
Applying ideal Raoult's law behavior to a solution known to deviate significantly (e.g. due to strong hydrogen bonding between different components).
genZNote: Raoult's law: vapour pressure is just mole fraction calling the shots.
